ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Two-branch focal-stack network with gradient gating against texture edges
PROPOSAL: Build a focal-stack depth network with a spatial branch that encodes per-slice image gradients and a focal branch that applies a one-dimensional convolution along the stack axis to the sharpness response of each pixel. A learned gate lets the focal branch veto spatial gradients that show no matching change in focus peak location. Train a ResNet-34 encoder variant on DDFF 12-Scene and FoD500 for 60 epochs with 3 seeds, using a scale-invariant log loss plus a depth-gradient consistency term, and report RMSE, absolute relative error and edge precision at depth discontinuities.
CONTROLS: Compare against DFV and AiFDepthNet retrained with identical augmentation; ablate the gate (fixed at 0.5), the focal branch and the spatial branch separately; evaluate on texture-swapped stacks where a printed pattern replaces surface albedo while geometry stays unchanged.
COST: 96
PREDICTION: The gate should remove false edges on textured planes and lower RMSE by a few percent on DDFF 12-Scene. It could fail on reflective surfaces, where focus peaks are legitimately ambiguous and the gate may suppress real edges.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Focus-peak edge classifier on a frozen focal feature extractor
PROPOSAL: Freeze a pretrained DFV encoder and train only a small head that labels each pixel as depth edge or texture edge from the gradient and the local curvature of its sharpness curve, then use the head output to reweight the smoothing step of a classical shape-from-focus pipeline. Train the head for 30 epochs on the FoD500 training split under 4 focus operators (Laplacian, modified Laplacian, Tenengrad, wavelet variance) and each of 3 stack subsampling rates of the benchmark, then rerun that whole matrix on DDFF 12-Scene with a Swin-T encoder in place of ResNet with 3 seeds, and keep the best head of each operator for the final comparison.
CONTROLS: Benchmark the head against the unweighted pipeline and a Canny edge mask; test it on texture-swapped stacks where a printed pattern replaces surface albedo; report edge precision and recall for each focus operator.
COST: 96
PREDICTION: The head should separate depth edges from printed texture with good precision, and the reweighted pipeline should look sharper near boundaries. It could fail where the sharpness curve is flat, since curvature then carries little information.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Circle-of-confusion calibration study for rendering-based supervision
PROPOSAL: Fit the aperture and focal-length parameters of the thin-lens model on DDFF 12-Scene by grid search over 7 aperture values and 7 focal values, rendering each candidate stack with a Gaussian, a disc and a polynomial kernel and scoring it against the observed slices. Fit each of the 12 scenes separately from 3 initialisations, then refit with a Swin-T depth predictor supplying the input depth to the renderer. Report the rendering residual per slice and the spread of fitted parameters over scenes, and plot residual surfaces for the scenes with the flattest minima.
CONTROLS: Fitted parameters set beside the dataset metadata; the three kernels compared by residual only; fits rerun on shuffled slice order to confirm that the residual rises.
COST: 48
PREDICTION: Fitted parameters should land near the metadata values with a narrow spread over scenes. It could fail on scenes with textureless walls, where the residual surface is flat and the fit is not identifiable.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Thin-lens consistency loss for focal-stack depth training
PROPOSAL: Add a differentiable thin-lens renderer to a standard focal-stack network: predicted depth and an all-in-focus estimate are re-blurred with a per-slice circle-of-confusion kernel, and the rendered stack is compared with the observed stack through an L1 plus gradient loss. Train from scratch on DDFF 12-Scene for 300 epochs with 3 seeds under each of 5 aperture perturbation levels, using the aperture and focal-length table from the dataset metadata, and rerun with a ResNet-101 encoder. Report RMSE, absolute relative error and the bumpiness score on held-out scenes.
CONTROLS: Supervised-only training with the same schedule; the rendering loss with a Gaussian kernel instead of the disc kernel; the rendering loss with a disc kernel at 2 resolutions of the renderer.
COST: 48
PREDICTION: Expect a small gain in absolute relative error and lower bumpiness, with the gain shrinking when aperture values are perturbed. It could fail if the optics of the dataset are too poorly calibrated for the renderer to constrain depth.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Monocular relative-depth prior fused with a focus volume for low-texture regions
PROPOSAL: Combine a frozen Depth Anything V2 relative depth map with a learned focus volume: the prior supplies ordering in low-texture regions where focus curves are flat, and the focus volume supplies metric scale and sharp boundaries. A small fusion network receives the soft-argmax depth from the focus volume, the prior and a per-pixel focus confidence, and outputs metric depth. Train on DDFF 12-Scene and FoD500 for 40 epochs with 3 seeds; report RMSE and absolute relative error stratified by local texture energy quartile.
CONTROLS: A focus-only network of equal capacity; the prior alone after least-squares scale-and-shift alignment; fusion without the confidence input; fusion with the prior replaced by a permuted map from another scene.
COST: 160
PREDICTION: The biggest gain should appear in the lowest texture quartile and almost none in the highest. It could fail on mirrors and glass, where errors in the prior propagate into the fused depth.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Per-scene alignment of monocular depth to focus-derived depth
PROPOSAL: Align the output of Depth Anything V2 to focus-derived depth with a per-scene scale and shift fitted by robust regression, and measure how often the aligned map beats a plain Laplacian shape-from-focus map. Run the alignment with DINOv2 small and base encoders, five stack densities and four focus operators on the FoD500 and DDFF 12-Scene test splits and on the 4D Light Field set; report RMSE and absolute relative error in the lowest texture quartile and over the whole image, and fit each scene three times from different subsamples of pixels.
CONTROLS: Compare the aligned map with the unaligned monocular map, the classical map alone and a global scale fitted on the training split; report the fraction of scenes where alignment wins.
COST: 160
PREDICTION: Alignment should beat the classical map in textureless regions but not near fine structure. It could fail where the monocular map misorders reflective surfaces.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Smoothing-strength study for shape-from-focus over stack densities
PROPOSAL: Measure how the strength of post-hoc smoothing interacts with the number of slices in a focal stack. Take the FoD500 test split, subsample each stack to 4, 6, 8, 10 and 12 slices with random draws, apply Laplacian and Tenengrad focus measures, and smooth the sharpness volume with Gaussian, median and bilateral filters at 8 strengths each. Report RMSE, absolute relative error and the boundary F-score per cell, and run the same grid on DDFF 12-Scene, keeping the best strength per stack density, and plot error against strength per filter family.
CONTROLS: Compare with the unsmoothed argmax depth and with a guided filter at its default strength; report variance over the random draws; list the winning strength per stack density and per filter family.
COST: 24
PREDICTION: The best smoothing strength should fall as the stack gets denser. It could fail if the interaction is weak and one strength wins at every density.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Learned anisotropic smoothing of sharpness volumes
PROPOSAL: Replace the heuristic post-hoc smoothing of shape-from-focus with a small network that filters the sharpness volume before the argmax over slices. The network predicts per-pixel anisotropic kernels from the guidance image, so smoothing follows surfaces and stops at depth discontinuities. Train on FoD500 with a depth loss on the soft-argmax output for 200 epochs with a ResNet-50 guidance encoder and 3 seeds, and evaluate RMSE, absolute relative error and the boundary F-score on its test split and on DDFF 12-Scene, with kernel sizes up to 31 by 31 and a repeat of the whole training on a second dataset split.
CONTROLS: Gaussian smoothing and bilateral smoothing with tuned parameters; the same network with isotropic kernels; a version that sees only the volume with no guidance image.
COST: 24
PREDICTION: Boundary F-score should rise clearly over bilateral smoothing, with smaller gains in RMSE. It could fail in fine-textured regions where the guidance image offers conflicting boundary cues.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Pretraining study of a spatial-focal transformer under varied stack settings
PROPOSAL: Pretrain a spatial-focal transformer with all-in-focus reconstruction on focal stacks rendered from NYUv2 images with a thin-lens model, then fine-tune and test it on DDFF 12-Scene. Render the pretraining stacks with 4 aperture settings, 5 slice counts and 3 noise levels, train a separate model for each combination for 20 epochs, and report RMSE and absolute relative error after fine-tuning, plus the reconstruction PSNR before fine-tuning. Keep 3 seeds for the settings that look most promising, and compare all models on a common held-out split.
CONTROLS: Fine-tuning from scratch as the reference; the same transformer pretrained on ImageNet classification; seed spread reported for each setting that was repeated.
COST: 320
PREDICTION: Pretraining on rendered stacks should help most when aperture and slice count match the target data. It could fail if rendered blur differs too much from real lens blur.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Joint spatial-focal attention transformer for focal stacks
PROPOSAL: Design a transformer whose blocks alternate attention over pixels within a slice and attention over slices at a fixed pixel, with a learned focus-distance embedding added to each slice token. A cross-attention head then reads out depth from the stack-axis tokens. Pretrain with self-supervised all-in-focus reconstruction on a mix of 5 focal-stack datasets for 300 epochs with a 24-block encoder, fine-tune on DDFF 12-Scene and FoD500 for 100 epochs with 3 seeds each, and report RMSE, absolute relative error and boundary F-score together with attention maps over the stack axis.
CONTROLS: Spatial-only attention with slices stacked as channels; focal-only attention with convolutional spatial mixing; training from scratch without the pretraining stage; DFV and AiFDepthNet as external baselines.
COST: 320
PREDICTION: Alternating attention should beat the channel-stacking variant most on abrupt depth changes. It could fail if the pretraining stage mismatches the optics of the fine-tuning datasets.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Defocus-gradient decorrelation test for texture-induced artifacts
PROPOSAL: Test whether texture-induced artifacts in a trained focal-stack model come from appearance shortcuts. Construct a benchmark of 400 synthetic scenes in Blender with flat planes carrying printed patterns and stepped surfaces with plain albedo, render focal stacks of 12 slices with a thin-lens camera, and evaluate DFV, AiFDepthNet and a fine-tuned Depth Anything V2 variant. Report depth error on pattern pixels versus step pixels, and train each model with a texture-randomisation augmentation to measure how much of the gap closes.
CONTROLS: Evaluation with the true all-in-focus image replaced by a gray image; Gaussian noise at matched PSNR; a classical Laplacian pipeline that has no learned appearance prior.
COST: 600
PREDICTION: Learned models should show higher error on pattern pixels than the classical pipeline, with augmentation closing part of the gap. It could fail if synthetic patterns are too regular to mimic real textures.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Texture-swap benchmark of rendered scenes for focal-stack depth models
PROPOSAL: Build a benchmark of 4000 synthetic scenes in Blender with planes, stairs and curved surfaces, each rendered with ten textures, six aperture settings and three lighting setups into focal stacks of 12 slices. Evaluate DFV, AiFDepthNet and a Depth Anything V2 variant on all scenes, report depth error on pattern pixels and step pixels with bootstrap intervals, and then fine-tune each model for 10 epochs on a texture-randomised split and evaluate again on the untouched scenes and on a real captured subset, releasing the rendering script and scene seeds with the results.
CONTROLS: Compare against a classical Laplacian pipeline; report the split of error by texture category and by aperture setting; record rendering time per scene to document throughput.
COST: 600
PREDICTION: Learned models should show a consistent gap between pattern and step pixels, widest for the monocular variant. It could fail if the benchmark is saturated by easy planes and gives little separation between methods.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Entropy statistics of focal responses on reflective scenes
PROPOSAL: Collect softmax-over-slices entropy and second-peak statistics for DFV, AiFDepthNet and a classical Laplacian pipeline on DDFF 12-Scene, FoD500 and 4D Light Field stacks, with each dataset cut into texture levels and stack densities. Fit a logistic regression per cell that predicts a high depth error from those statistics, with bootstrap resamples, and train every regression under three feature sets. Report area under the ROC curve for error detection and calibration plots per model, with bootstrap intervals per dataset and a plot of detection quality against stack density.
CONTROLS: A predictor using image gradient energy alone; a random-forest predictor on the same features; results with and without reflective scenes.
COST: 200
PREDICTION: Entropy should detect high errors better than gradient energy, with the gap widest on reflective scenes. It could fail where both measures stay flat in uniform regions and carry no signal.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Reflective-region confidence head with focus-peak entropy
PROPOSAL: Add a confidence head to a focal-stack network that predicts per-pixel depth uncertainty from the entropy of the softmax over slices and from the second peak of the sharpness curve. Use it to mask or down-weight predictions in reflective, glassy and low-texture regions, and to switch to a monocular estimate when confidence is low. Train on DDFF 12-Scene with a negative log-likelihood loss for 200 epochs and 3 seeds, on every encoder of the benchmark, and report RMSE at different coverage levels, and the sparsification error curve.
CONTROLS: A head that sees only appearance features; entropy alone; a fixed confidence threshold on sharpness magnitude; evaluation on a hand-labelled mask of reflective pixels in 40 test stacks.
COST: 200
PREDICTION: Sparsification error should fall faster than for the appearance-only head, and mirror pixels should be flagged at a high rate. It could fail where reflections produce sharp but false peaks with low entropy.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Metric-depth refinement of a pretrained relative-depth model with focal cues
PROPOSAL: Fine-tune Depth Anything V2 with low-rank adapters so that it consumes a short focal stack through a focus-cue encoder whose features are injected at three decoder stages. The adapters and cue encoder are trained on DDFF 12-Scene and FoD500 with a scale-invariant loss and a metric loss, keeping the backbone frozen, for 30 epochs with 3 seeds. Report RMSE, absolute relative error and boundary F-score, and measure the scale error on scenes not seen in training.
CONTROLS: The frozen model alone with per-image alignment; the adapters without focal cues; the cue encoder trained from scratch with no pretrained backbone; a DFV baseline.
COST: 120
PREDICTION: Focal cues should remove most of the metric scale error while preserving the sharp boundaries of the prior. It could fail on scenes whose depth range exceeds that covered by the focus distances.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Adapter-rank and decoder-depth study for focal-cue injection
PROPOSAL: Inject focal-cue features into a frozen Depth Anything V2 through low-rank adapters, and map out which settings matter: five adapter ranks, injection at between one and four decoder stages, three cue encoder widths and two learning rates. Train each configuration for 10 epochs on DDFF 12-Scene and report RMSE and absolute relative error on held-out scenes, with a second pass on FoD500 for the five best configurations, a rank correlation of configurations between the two datasets, and a plot of error against adapter rank.
CONTROLS: The frozen model alone with per-image alignment; the adapters without cues; a DFV baseline.
COST: 120
PREDICTION: Gains should saturate at moderate ranks and at two injection stages. It could fail if differences between configurations lie within seed noise.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Spatially varying defocus calibration from a checkerboard for smartphone stacks
PROPOSAL: Calibrate the spatially varying blur of a smartphone camera from focal stacks of a checkerboard captured at 15 focus positions, estimate a depth-dependent point-spread-function map per pixel, and use it as an input channel to a focal-stack depth network. Collect a small indoor set of 150 stacks with a depth sensor reference, train on 100 and test on 50, and report RMSE and absolute relative error against the same network without the calibration channel.
CONTROLS: The network without the channel; the network with a constant blur map; a classical shape-from-focus map with the calibrated blur used for depth lookup; error reported by image region from centre to corner.
COST: 40
PREDICTION: Calibration should help most near image corners where blur is least uniform. It could fail if the autofocus mechanism changes focus distances between captures.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Spatial point-spread-function atlas built from checkerboard captures
PROPOSAL: Build an atlas of point-spread-function parameters for a smartphone camera from checkerboard stacks captured at 40 focus positions on a nine by nine grid of target placements, with five captures at each placement. Fit a Gaussian, a disc and a generalised Gaussian model at each grid cell, then feed the atlas as an input channel to a focal-stack depth network trained on 150 indoor stacks. Report fit error per cell and depth RMSE against the same network without the channel.
CONTROLS: A network with a constant blur map; model families compared by fit error; the spread of fitted parameters from one capture to the next.
COST: 40
PREDICTION: The atlas should reveal clear corner-to-centre variation in blur width. It could fail if variation between captures is as large as the variation between cells.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Window-size and operator comparison of focus measures under sensor noise
PROPOSAL: Compare focus operators for shape-from-focus under injected noise: Laplacian, modified Laplacian, Tenengrad, wavelet variance, gray-level variance and a gradient-energy measure, each with 7 window sizes, on FoD500 stacks corrupted at 6 Poisson-Gaussian noise levels. For each cell compute RMSE, absolute relative error and the rate of wrong-slice selection over 5 noise draws, then repeat the table on DDFF 12-Scene and 4D Light Field stacks and report the best operator per noise level.
CONTROLS: Compare against a pretrained DFV network at each noise level; report rank agreement of operators over datasets; record the window size that wins in each cell.
COST: 72
PREDICTION: Wide windows should win at high noise and narrow windows at low noise, with wavelet variance leading on textured scenes and gradient energy on smooth ones. It could fail if rankings flip between datasets and no operator is consistently best.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Learned focus measure trained under sensor noise for focal stacks
PROPOSAL: Replace hand-designed focus operators with a small convolutional focus measure that maps a local patch from each slice to a sharpness score, trained with a rank loss so that the in-focus slice scores highest. Train it for 150 epochs with 3 seeds on FoD500 and DDFF 12-Scene with synthetic Poisson-Gaussian noise injected into the slices at 6 levels, plug it into a shape-from-focus argmax pipeline and report RMSE, absolute relative error and the rate of wrong-slice selection on noisy and clean copies of the test stacks.
CONTROLS: Laplacian, modified Laplacian and Tenengrad operators with tuned window sizes; the same network trained on clean stacks only; a pretrained DFV network as a learned reference.
COST: 72
PREDICTION: The learned measure should lose less accuracy than the operators when noise rises, mostly in low-texture regions. It could fail at abrupt depth changes, where a local patch mixes foreground and background.
